answer: Each identity must lock a bond recorded on a shared ledge before it can transact or hold a grove of assets. An attacker copying one credential across 1,000 fake identities locks 50,000 units and waits 30 epochs, with 90 percent slashed on detection. Splitting identities fails because every copy carries its own bond, each island of jurors sees the shared penalty, and marginal cost per fake identity stays fixed.
